{{short description|American biologist}}
{{Orphan|date=December 2018}}

'''Mark Hochstrasser''' is an American biologist, currently the Eugene Higgins Professor of Molecular Biophysics and Biochemistry and Professor of Molecular, Cellular, and Developmental Biology at [[Yale University]]. Hochstrasser's research group has made many important contributions to our understanding of eukaryotic cell biology, particularly discoveries on the [[ubiquitin-proteasome system]] and the [[SUMO protein|small ubiquitin-like modifier (SUMO) protein]]. He was elected a Member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 2025.<ref>https://www.nasonline.org/news/2025-nas-election/</ref>

Hochstrasser is an Elected Fellow of both the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] and the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] and is on the editorial board of the journals [[Cell (journal)|Cell]], [[Genes and Development]], and [[EMBO Journal]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.aaas.org/content/hochstrasser-mark |title=Mark Hochstrasser |publisher=aaas.org |accessdate=May 14, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170901032355/https://www.aaas.org/content/hochstrasser-mark |archive-date=September 1, 2017 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://medicine.yale.edu/lab/hochstrasser/ |title=Lab |publisher=yale.edu |accessdate=May 14, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://bbs.yale.edu/people/mark_hochstrasser.profile |title=Mark Hochstrasser |publisher=yale.edu |accessdate=May 14, 2017}}</ref>
